name: Flight jackets

card.summary: Bomber and aviator-style jackets, originally military cold-weather gear, worn to add shoulder structure, a cropped waist and a classic masculine silhouette.

quick.overview:
Flight jackets are waist-length jackets that began as warm outerwear for open-cockpit pilots and are now an everyday fashion staple. Models such as the A-2, G-1, B-3 and MA-1 are the best known.

For appearance, the short cut, ribbed cuffs and waistband create a defined waist and structured shoulder line, a look many men use to read as put-together. Their history and design are documented; no study measures their effect on attractiveness.
quick.how: People wear them as a layering piece over tees, knits or hoodies. Leather A-2 and G-1 styles, shearling B-3 styles and nylon MA-1 styles are the usual families, chosen for warmth, colour and fit.
quick.risks: Low risk. Fit is the main practical issue, and leather and shearling versions cost more and need care. Authentic military-pattern pieces are sold as vintage or reproductions.

lead: A flight jacket, also called a bomber or aviator jacket, is a short outer garment developed for pilots flying in cold, open or unheated aircraft.[1][2]

The U.S. Army's Aviation Clothing Board began issuing heavy leather flight jackets in September 1917. The A-2 followed in 1931, the Navy's G-1 paralleled it, the B-3 became the Air Force shearling bomber, and the nylon MA-1, usually sage green with a blaze orange lining, is the model most people now associate with the term.[1]

Civilians adopted the style through scooterboy and skinhead subcultures, 1980s baseball-style bombers and early-2000s hip-hop fashion, and Raf Simons brought the MA-1 into high fashion in 2001, per Wikipedia.[1] For looks, the cropped length and snug cuffs shape the waist and shoulders.

chain: Defined waist and structured shoulder line
angle.text: The short cut and elastic hem emphasise the waist and shoulders, so the jacket works as a layering piece that frames the upper body.

infobox: Ribbed cuffs and waistband, zip front

paras: Classic features are a waist-length body, knit cuffs and hem, and a front zip. Leather versions use horsehide or goatskin, shearling versions add warmth, and the MA-1 uses nylon with an orange lining.[1][2]

Early pilots wore heavy coats against wind and cold; the Aviation Clothing Board was established in 1917 and set standards for leather flight jackets.[1] The jacket moved into mainstream wear through subcultures and fashion houses, and Top Gun reportedly raised G-1 sales.[1]
